children: Palm oil falls in Asian trading. Elevated inventories despite strong exports and fading seasonal demand are weighing on market sentiment, AmInvestment Bank says in a note. Consumption in Northern India is expected to ease during winter, while weaker Brent crude has narrowed palm oil's price discount to gasoil, reducing its appeal as a biofuel feedstock, it adds. AmInvestment Bank pegs support for crude palm oil futures at 4,300 ringgit a ton and resistance at 4,453 ringgit a ton. The Bursa Malaysia Derivatives contract for January delivery is 26 ringgit lower at 4,351 ringgit a ton. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
